issues.body: `run_nl_query` parses the completion, checks forbidden constructs, and returns it without running the default-enabled dictionary check that the real `Nlq::ask` loop performs. Consequently, a hallucinated predicate or class IRI absent from `graph` is accepted here even though `ask` would repair or reject it. This remains material because `crates/sparq-mcp/src/lib.rs` and `skills/agent-tools/SKILL.md` still describe `nl_query` as using the same grounded generation and validation as `ask`; the new syntax-only wording elsewhere does not make those public parity claims true. The added tests do not exercise an unknown graph term.
issues.fix_hint: Apply the same `config.check_dictionary` and `sparq_nlq::constrain::unknown_terms(graph, &parsed)` branch as `Nlq::ask`, use the dictionary repair message in the repair prompt, and add a test proving that an unknown predicate or class IRI is repaired or rejected. Alternatively, consistently remove the same-validation parity claim from every public doc and explicitly specify parse-plus-forbidden-construct validation only.
issues.title: Translate-only path still omits ask's dictionary validation

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant: the same major dictionary-grounding mismatch remains. `run_nl_query` still returns immediately after parse and forbidden-construct validation and never applies the default-enabled `config.check_dictionary` / `constrain::unknown_terms` validation used by `Nlq::ask`. Some prose now accurately calls validation syntactic, but the public crate docs and agent-tools skill still promise the same grounded generation and validation as `ask`, so an unknown predicate or class IRI can be returned despite that advertised parity. No test covers the missing dictionary-validation invariant.
